# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 7 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 7
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Understand therefore, children of joy, that the good Lord revealed all things to us beforehand, so that we might know to whom to give thanks and praise for all things.
2. If therefore the Son of God, who is Lord and who will come to judge the living and dead, suffered that his wounding might give us life — let us believe that the Son of God could not have suffered except on our account.
3. But also, when he was crucified, he was given gall and vinegar to drink. Hear how the priests of the temple have given a type of this: the commandment having been written: "Whoever does not keep the fast shall die the death" — the Lord commanded, because he was about to offer the vessel of the Spirit as a sacrifice for our sins, so that the type established in Isaac, who was offered upon the altar, might be fulfilled.
4. What then does he say in the prophet? "And they shall eat of the goat offered on the fast day for all sins." Hear carefully: "And let all the priests alone eat the entrails unwashed with vinegar."
5. Why? "Because you are going to give me gall and vinegar to drink when I am already on the point of offering my flesh for the sins of my new people" — therefore you alone shall eat, while the people fast and mourn in sackcloth and ashes, to show that he must suffer on their behalf.
6. Mark what was commanded: "Take two fine and similar goats, and offer them, and let the priest take the one as a burnt offering for sins."
7. And what shall they do with the other? "The other," he says, "is accursed." Observe how the type of Jesus appears here.
8. "And all of you shall spit on it and pierce it, and wind scarlet wool around its head, and so let it be cast out into the desert." And when this is done, the one who carries the goat leads it into the wilderness and takes away the wool, and places it upon a shrub which is called rachia — the plant from which we are accustomed to eat the shoots when we find them in the country, the fruit being sweet.
9. And so I understand why this is: when they see him coming on that day with his long scarlet robe flowing to his ankles, they shall say: "Is this not he whom we crucified — whose garment we despised and pierced, in whose side they thrust a lance? Truly this man was the Son of God."
10. For as they will be like him when he comes — but he will not be like them.
